chapter: Arrangements, repertoire and the last band
title: Rickard Alexis and Buddy Petit losing work by taking multiple deposits
summary: Laurent says Rickard Alexis and Buddy Petit lost jobs, including the Roosevelt, because they took several deposits for the same night.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Yeah. At one time. Before Dr. Louie Warnie was playing trombone with me. Louie Warnie. Then after I gave Doc a break. Nobody wouldn't hire Doc. I gave Doc a break. I put him back to work. Just like Rickard Alexis was down to the breaks. I had all the work around him. I had it. P-Rod was loafing. He's coming to me and begging me for jobs. So Rickard was down. Nobody wouldn't hire him. He was afraid. He'd take a deposit from you. He'd take a deposit from you. He'd take a deposit from you. And all that's on the same night. Now he couldn't fulfill them three jobs. So naturally they got so they wouldn't give him no work.
They said Buddy Petit was that way.

That's how Buddy Petit lost to Roosevelt. He was in the goal room. Really? I didn't know that. Well, sure. He'd play it up there with the same girl I'm talking to you about now. Helen Edwards. She was the pianist up there in the goal room at the Roosevelt. But that's how he lost that job. Taking two, three deposits. And he would go around and instead of going to the Roosevelt where he was making money, big money, he'd go around to them halls and play where he could get up and dance. You understand? Play two, three numbers and then he'd call you and say, say, play me two, three numbers in my place. They'd go out on the floor and dance. Well, that bust him up, he lost the rules for him. That tore him up. Big Illo, he played with me too. When Big Illo was playing C clarinet.
